text.brief: An orbital analyst at Vandenberg watches a mainland satellite drift to within 20 kilometers of an American missile-warning satellite in 2031. The same satellite has parked beside three others that year and left each time before anyone said a word.
text.record: Shijian-21 towed a dead Beidou satellite to a graveyard orbit in January 2022. Shijian-25 docked with Shijian-21 in geostationary orbit in July 2025 for the first apparent refueling there ([Secure World Foundation: Chinese RPO fact sheet](https://www.swfound.org/publications-and-reports/chinese-military-and-intelligence-rendezvous-and-proximity-operations-fact-sheet)). The two separated on November 25, 2025. The Space Force's vice chief said in March 2025 that five mainland satellites had practiced dogfighting in low orbit.
text.reading: The Party parks its inspectors next to America's most valuable satellites and watches the response. Silence teaches it that close approach is normal, and a crisis later finds its servicers already in place with arms that can grab or blind. This is Stratagem 13, stomp the grass to scare the snake.
text.coreEvent: American officials report in public that a mainland satellite closed within 10 kilometers of an American national security satellite in geostationary orbit before 2034.
text.gapText: Technology Architecture. America's key satellites are few, large and unable to move out of the way.
text.fix: Publish every close approach and field satellites that can move.
